key_insight: Near-teacher in-distribution performance after on-policy distillation can mask lost out-of-distribution capabilities and incomplete multi-teacher consolidation.
engineering_relevance: Evaluate consolidated models on extrapolative and composed tasks rather than treating strong in-distribution scores as proof of capability retention.
method: Test OPD and multi-teacher OPD using synthetic reasoning and Qwen3 models across math, coding, agent, and long-context tasks.
Investigate teacher capability, data coverage, and update geometry as factors in generalization gaps.
Propose geometry-based patching and base-preserving replay to improve OOD retention.
evidence_signal: Across extrapolative settings, distilled models reached 96.04–102.73% of teacher IND scores but scored 2.45–16.25% below the base model on OOD tasks; across three compositional settings, MOPD scored 18.19–24.34% below the best teachers on composed OOD tasks.
watch_item: Jointly improving teacher capability and data coverage eliminated OOD forgetting in the reported experiments, but this does not establish reliable retention on unseen task distributions.
paper_title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
